headword: {往生際|おうじょうぎわ}が{悪|わる}い
reading: おうじょうぎわがわるい
gloss: refusing to give up; being a poor loser

definitions.gloss: refusing to give up; being a poor loser; not accepting defeat gracefully
definitions.explanation: Stubbornly refusing to accept an inevitable outcome or admit defeat. Literally 'bad at the moment of death,' from the Buddhist concept of dying peacefully.

examples.japanese: {往生際|おうじょうぎわ}が{悪|わる}いぞ。
examples.english: Stop being such a poor loser.

examples.japanese: ⟦{証拠|しょうこ}→証拠：10575_shouko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{往生際|おうじょうぎわ}が{悪|わる}く⟦{否認|ひにん}→否認：11961_hinin⟧し⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧た。
examples.english: Despite the evidence, he stubbornly continued to deny it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{負|ま}け→負け：02569_make⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{認|みと}め→認める：02429_mitomeru⟧ず⟦{言|い}い{訳|わけ}→言い訳：04653_iiwake⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{往生際|おうじょうぎわ}が{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: Not admitting defeat and making excuses all the time is being a poor loser.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
From Buddhist terminology: ⟦{往生|おうじょう}→往生：12704_oujou⟧ means passing on to the Pure Land (dying peacefully), and {際|ぎわ} means the moment of. Someone with a 'bad' {往生際|おうじょうぎわ} cannot accept their fate and clings desperately to life — extended figuratively to anyone who refuses to accept an inevitable outcome.

USAGE:
Used to criticize someone who won't gracefully accept defeat, admit wrongdoing, or give up when the situation is clearly hopeless. Often said directly to the person.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {往生際|おうじょうぎわ}が{悪|わる}い⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a person who can't accept defeat)
- {往生際|おうじょうぎわ}⟦{悪|わる}く→悪い：00908_warui⟧⟦{抵抗|ていこう}する→抵抗する：15888_teikousuru⟧ (to stubbornly resist)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{潔|いさぎよ}くない→潔い：07315_isagiyoi⟧: ungraceful — refusing to accept things cleanly
- {悪|わる}あがき: desperate struggle — futile resistance
